newsitem.title: GREECE: OLYMPIC AIRWAYS SEES 97 PRETAX PROFIT UP 35PCT.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPIC AIRWAYS SEES 97 PRETAX PROFIT UP 35PCT.

text.p: Olympic Airways told a news conference on Wednesday that its 1996 pretax profit was estimated at 10 billion drachmas, up 0.1 percent from 9.9 billion a year earlier.
"We also expect 1997 pretax profits to rise 35 percent to 13.5 billion drachmas, from 10 billion in 1996," said Iordanis Karatzas, managing director at Olympic Airways.
Passenger numbers were also better in 1996. In the domestic market, there was a 9.8 percent increase in the number of passengers, to 2.619 million from 2.385 million in 1995.
Foreign passengers rose 9.4 percent to 2.471 million from 2.258 million in 1995, he said.
"In early 1996 the EU issued a report saying Olympic's operation was improving and that in the near future it would be able to proceed without state subsidising," he said.

The implementation of a new organisational structure, expected to have a positive impact on the revenues of Olympic Airways, will be completed by end-May and more information will then be released, said Olympic Airways president Nikolaos Blesios.
An important investment step will be the addition to of another four aircraft to its fleet of 33 by the end of the year, he added.
There were preliminary agreements with Air Bus and Boeing for a total order of $378 million, he said.
Olympic Airways is also negotiating with Malev and Air Ukraine on Balkan routes, he added.
The cooperation of Olumpic Airways with a major U.S. airline is expected to be completed before this summer, he said.

"Our company is already in talks with TWA. Olympic will cover the international part of flights from Athens to U.S. destinations and TWA will service the U.S. connecting flights," he added. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
